newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 26.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 26.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.
LONDON - UK shares were closed on Monday for a market holiday. On Friday the FTSE 100 index ended 10.0 higher at 4,661.8.

FRANKFURT - German shares shrugged off early nerves following the unexpected left-wing victory in the French parliamentary elections to surge to fresh record highs in bourse trade, albeit on thin volumes.
The blue chip DAX index surged past old records to end the bourse session up 55.67 points at 3,657.86 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX stood at 3,669.31 up 47.59 points.

PARIS - French stocks plunged to their biggest single-day loss in more than four years on Monday after the left won the first round of the parliamentary election. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 108.16 points, at 2,654.74. That was its largest fall, in percentage terms, since October 1992 when it lost 3.97 percent in one session, according to the stockmarkets association SBF.

ZURICH - A late slide in Roche certificates wiped out most of the market's early gains, but the indices still ended at a new record close. Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche said the purchase of Boehringer Mannheim Group for around $11 billion would cause a significant dilution of earlings in the first year. "After this, the stock came down rapidly," one trader noted. Sentiment remained optimistic, one dealer said. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 11.83 points, to 3,284.68.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed marginally higher on Monday helped by buying of a limited number of issues, backed partly by solid corporate earnings reports. Market participants were still cautious over the currency market and Wall Street stocks.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 34.50 points to finish the session at 20,043.50.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soared to a record closing high on record turnover on Monday as overseas money continued to flow in looking to snap up big cap stocks and red chips. The blue-chip index rose 242.96 points to close at 14,574.64, a touch off the intra-day high of 14,581.35.

SYDNEY - The Australia share market ended with its fourth straight record close on Monday, climbing solidly in response to a Dow jump on Friday and ignoring a fall in its biggest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd .
The All Ordinaries Index finished up 20.9 points at 2,584.8 which was also its intra-day high and its all-time record high, eclipsing Friday's record mark of 2,572.7 by 12.1 points.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares shed small territory after subdued trade on Monday with Standard Bank shares hit by news New Age Beverages (NAB) owes it 230 million rand and had applied for voluntary liquidation last week.
The overall index was down 4.2 points at 7,067.5 points, the industrial index was up 7.5 points to 8,319.6 points and the gold index ended off 3.1 points at 1,189.1 points.
